title: Redwood data retention & PII controls demo - Silvercove Payments

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-14
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Brian Lowe (CTO, Silvercove), Maya Singh (Head of Security), Elliot Park (Compliance)

Auto-summary: quick walkthrough of data retention and redaction features across API and Console, demo of toggles to disable request storage, and discussion of KMS integration and audit logging.

[00:00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everybody, thanks for joining, uh, appreciate you making time. Quick intro — I'm Alex Chen, account exec, and with me is Priya, our solutions engineer who will run the demo.
[00:00:12] Brian Lowe: Hi Alex, hi Priya, thanks. Brian here. We have Maya and Elliot with us as well. We'll stay mostly quiet but ask questions.
[00:00:18] Maya Singh: Hey all. We're primarily interested in how Redwood handles PII, whether we can turn off request storage for production, and how keys work with KMS.
[00:00:24] Elliot Park: Also retention by customer/tenant - we need per-tenant retention windows for audit.
[00:00:30] Alex Chen: Yep totally, that's what this demo is for. Priya, do you want to kick off with the Console and then show the API flags?
[00:00:36] Priya Kapoor: Sure, thanks Alex. I'm going to share my screen — if anyone can't see, let me know.
[00:00:48] [screen share starts]
[00:00:52] Priya Kapoor: So here is the Redwood Console — top nav, we have Observability, Models, and Settings. Under Settings -> Data & Retention we expose retention policies at org, project, and route level. You can set retention windows, e.g. 30d, 90d, indefinite, or custom.
[00:01:10] Brian Lowe: Quick q: can retention be set per customer tenant? We have multi-tenant data separation requirements.
[00:01:17] Priya Kapoor: Yes — you can target retention via route tags or tenant IDs. In our Dedicated and Private offerings we also support VPC-scoped policies. The UI shows a 'apply to' dropdown — org/project/route/tenant.
[00:01:32] Maya Singh: And is that enforced at ingestion or during retention jobs? We need assurance it is never written to logs past the window.
[00:01:40] Priya Kapoor: Good question — we have both: an ingest-time policy that can prevent storage when toggled, and periodic retention sweeps. For high-security tenants you can enable request-storage toggle which prevents persisting request bodies to disk and only stores minimal metadata for billing and metrics.
[00:01:58] Elliot Park: Minimal metadata meaning tokens, model used, latency? Anything that could include PII?
[00:02:04] Priya Kapoor: Minimal metadata is primarily token counts, model name, timestamps, and route ID. It does not include request text when request-storage is off. There is also an edge-case for streaming responses where KV cache keys are not stored.
[00:02:16] Brian Lowe: Ok that helps. How about automatic PII detection or redaction?
[00:02:22] Priya Kapoor: We include a redaction rules engine in the Console under Optimize -> Redaction. It can run pattern-based rules, regex, and ML-based PII detectors. You can choose to mask, hash, or redact fields.
[00:02:34] Priya Kapoor: For example, we ship a default PII set — emails, SSNs, credit cards — and you can add custom patterns per tenant. There's also a preview mode that runs on historical data in a sandbox so you can tune rules.
[00:02:46] Maya Singh: Are the ML detectors running inside our VPC for Private deployments?
[00:02:51] Priya Kapoor: Yes. For Private or Dedicated customers the detection can run on-prem or inside the customer's VPC. We also support bringing-your-own-detector if you have a preferred model.
[00:03:00] Alex Chen: Quick note — when you bring your own detector you can keep the model weights on your side and only send metadata to Redwood.
[00:03:06] Brian Lowe: Good. Walk me through the API toggle — like how would I disable storing request text programmatically?
[00:03:12] Priya Kapoor: Sure. In the API you can set the header X-Redwood-Store-Request: false or in SDK set request_storage=false. That flag tells the runtime not to persist the request body. If you set store_request=false and also enable redaction rules, the redaction is applied in-memory before any telemetry is emitted.
[00:03:30] Elliot Park: Does that affect billing accuracy? We need to reconcile token billing.
[00:03:35] Priya Kapoor: No — token accounting is separate and still accurate. We store token counts and costs for billing even when request storage is off. We can provide hashed request fingerprints for deduping without storing the raw content.
[00:03:46] Maya Singh: What about audit logs — we need an immutable audit trail of who changed retention policies and access.
[00:03:52] Priya Kapoor: We have an Audit Logs section — it records policy changes, user actions, deployments, SDK key rotations. Logs can be exported to your SIEM or to a storage bucket; entries are signed and include actor, timestamp, and diffs. For Private deployments exports can be configured to go to your S3 or GS bucket using customer-side KMS.
[00:04:10] Brian Lowe: KMS — do you support AWS KMS and customer-managed keys?
[00:04:14] Priya Kapoor: Yes, we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault. For Dedicated and Private we support HSM integrations and customer-managed keys. Keys are never stored in plaintext on Redwood's control plane.
[00:04:26] Maya Singh: Is the encryption at rest for stored requests under our KMS?
[00:04:29] Priya Kapoor: For private and dedicated, yes — data at rest is encrypted using your CMKs. For hosted customers we use Redwood-managed keys by default, but you can opt into BYOK for specific contracts.
[00:04:40] Alex Chen: I'll note that for enterprise deals we typically do BYOK with HSM key wrapping in the dedicated/private posture.
[00:04:46] [00:04:48] Priya Kapoor: Switching to a demo — here's the Optimize -> Redaction page. You can create rule sets and attach them to routes. I'll create a rule: credit_card -> mask last 4 digits. Apply to route 'silvercove-payments/transactions'.
[00:05:10] [keystrokes/background noise]
[00:05:18] Priya Kapoor: Now I'll show the API example. Post to /v1/generate with header X-Redwood-Store-Request: false. You can also set retention_window=30d as a per-request override when needed.
[00:05:30] Brian Lowe: Is per-request override auditable? We need to see who did it.
[00:05:34] Priya Kapoor: Yes, overrides show up in Audit Logs with the user or API key that made the change and the override reason if provided.
[00:05:40] Maya Singh: On the topic of logs, sometimes transcription systems mangle product names. Do you keep original verbatim transcripts of customer audio for debugging?
[00:05:48] Alex Chen: Audio transcripts are a separate product, but same controls apply — you can disable transcript storage or set redaction masks. For production, most customers disable raw transcript storage and only keep anonymized telemetry.
[00:05:59] Elliot Park: We saw references in your docs to a 'KV cache' — is there any risk of sensitive keys or tokens being persisted in that cache?
[00:06:06] Priya Kapoor: The KV cache only stores model key-value activations, not customer tokens or secrets. We also scrub any header-like patterns before writing caches to disk. For extra safety you can enable in-memory-only mode which disables persistent cache snapshots.
[00:06:20] Brian Lowe: Nice. How granular is RBAC — can we restrict who can change redaction rules?
[00:06:26] Priya Kapoor: RBAC is role-based and policy-driven. We have built-in roles (Admin, Security, Dev, Billing) and you can create custom roles with permission filters. You can also require SSO and MFA for policy changes.
[00:06:36] Maya Singh: For compliance we'll need separation of duties — change approval flows for retention and redaction rules.
[00:06:41] Priya Kapoor: We support approval workflows — policy changes can be set to require a second approver. All approvals are recorded in the Audit Log and in the policy history.
[00:06:50] [00:06:55] Alex Chen: Quick poll — does this align with the security posture you're expecting?
[00:06:59] Brian Lowe: So far yes, curious about legal/regulatory: data residency for EU customers.
[00:07:05] Priya Kapoor: We have region-aware routing and storage. For EU-only requirements we can route and persist data only in EU regions and disable cross-region backups. For private deployments you can opt for on-prem.
[00:07:16] Maya Singh: If we do a POC, we want a scoped environment with request-storage off and redaction rules applied — plus the ability to test with our sample payloads.
[00:07:24] Alex Chen: Totally reasonable. We'll propose a POC plan. Priya, can you outline a minimal POC?
[00:07:30] Priya Kapoor: Minimal POC: 1) Sandbox project in a dedicated tenant with retention=30d, request_storage=false; 2) Apply your redaction rules and run 1k sample calls; 3) Provide logs and redaction reports; 4) Run a short audit log export test. We'll need sample payloads and a contact for infra setup.
[00:07:47] Elliot Park: Timeline for that? We want it week of 5/25.
[00:07:50] Priya Kapoor: We can do that if we get payloads by 5/20 — we'll provision the sandbox and send instructions.
[00:07:57] Brian Lowe: Ok good. A few nitty-gritty questions: how do you handle backups? If request_storage is off, are backups still containing payloads?
[00:08:05] Priya Kapoor: Backups respect the request_storage setting; backups do not contain request bodies if the flag was set at write time. Backups do contain metadata for billing and tracing.
[00:08:15] Maya Singh: For legal holds, can we override retention to keep specific request IDs indefinitely?
[00:08:20] Priya Kapoor: We support legal hold tagging — when you tag an item with legal_hold=true it's excluded from retention sweeps. Access to remove legal holds requires privileged role and is logged.
[00:08:29] Alex Chen: We're close to the top of the hour — want to surface any blockers?
[00:08:33] Brian Lowe: Main blockers: SOC2 evidence and ability to do BYOK/HSM for production. Also cost for Dedicated vs hosted — but we'll discuss pricing separately.
[00:08:42] Alex Chen: Understood. We'll send over SOC2, an enterprise security pack, and sample BYOK docs. Priya will include config snippets.
[00:08:50] [00:08:55] Priya Kapoor: One more demo bit — API snippet for SDK: const client = new Redwood({apiKey: KEY, requestStorage: false, retentionWindow: '30d'}); then client.generate(...). The SDK will surface a warning if you try to set retention longer than org policy.
[00:09:10] Maya Singh: Can we get the SDK snippet in the repo or as a gist?
[00:09:13] Priya Kapoor: Yes I'll drop it in the thread.
[00:09:18] Alex Chen: Ok lets go through a couple of quick Qs from Elliot...
[00:09:22] Elliot Park: For compliance artifacts, do you provide attestations for encryption, key rotation, and penetration test results?
[00:09:27] Priya Kapoor: We provide SOC2 Type II reports, penetration test summaries, and key rotation policies. For dedicated clients we can provide additional artifacts under NDA.
[00:09:36] Brian Lowe: Anything else — latency impact of enabling redaction and request_storage=false?
[00:09:42] Priya Kapoor: In-memory redaction is low overhead, typically 5-15ms per request depending on rules. Disabling persistent storage slightly reduces tail latency since write I/O is avoided. There is a small CPU cost for ML-based PII detectors; we can offload that to a separate service or run it async if needed.
[00:09:58] Maya Singh: That's acceptable.
[00:10:01] [00:10:05] Alex Chen: Great. Recap and next steps: I'll send SOC2/security pack and pricing. Priya will send API/SDK snippets and Terraform/Console screenshots. We'll schedule POC kickoff for week of 5/25 pending payloads from Brian.
[00:10:18] Brian Lowe: Sounds good. One last ask — can you include an example of the redaction preview output so we can show legal/compliance?
[00:10:24] Priya Kapoor: Yes — I'll export a sample PDF showing before/after redaction and a rule-by-rule match count.
[00:10:31] Maya Singh: Thanks everyone.
[00:10:33] Alex Chen: Thanks y'all. We'll follow up in email.

[End of transcript — note: timestamps after 00:10 indicate the interactive portion; call total ~42 minutes including Q/A and follow-ups, recording clipped for brevity in transcript export.]
